blocks.text: The chapter’s final gathering at Hebron presents David’s kingship as receiving recognition from “all Israel.” The tribal contingents, their leaders, and the shared celebration underscore the breadth of that gathering. In Chronicles’ account, this recognition of David is paired with Jerusalem becoming the shared royal center.

“All Israel” should not be read as either a narrow biological label or a claim that every group was present in exactly the same way. Chronicles includes Judah-centered institutions while repeatedly incorporating northern and Transjordanian tribes; the long list in this chapter reflects that broad, though varied, picture of Israel gathering around David.
